mainTopic: Timing of חפיפה before טבילה, and the status of a נדה who skipped her twilight check
overview: The amud opens by finishing a story in which רב נחמן בר יצחק tells a woman to wash her hair that night and immerse right away. רבא then teaches that a woman may wash on ערב שבת and immerse on מוצאי שבת. רב פפא objects with a letter from רבין saying the opposite, because טבילה must come close to חפיפה. רבא publicly admits his mistake and teaches the correct ruling in רבי יוחנן's name. The גמרא then resolves two rulings that seem to clash: she washes by day when that is possible, and at night when it is not, as after שבת. A new משנה follows about a נדה who skipped the twilight check on her seventh day. If her morning check was clean she is presumed pure, and if it showed blood she is presumed impure, with views from רבי יהודה and the חכמים. Finally, the גמרא shows that the dispute of רב and לוי (definite זבה or doubtful זבה) is about a separate case where she was found impure both before and after, and explains each side's reasoning.

steps.title: The story ends: Why not wash your hair tonight?
steps.stepSummary: The woman in the story tells רב נחמן בר יצחק to come back tomorrow, hinting she had not washed her hair by day. He answers: do you lack kettles, buckets or servants? In other words, just wash tonight.
steps.simpleTranslation: She said: It is enough, come tomorrow. He understood what she meant, and said: Are you missing kettles? Are you missing buckets? Are you missing servants?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes a story that shows רב נחמן בר יצחק's view on when a woman may wash her hair before טבילה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: She wanted to put off her טבילה because she had not washed her hair during the day. He tells her she has everything she needs to heat water and wash right now, at night. So he holds that washing at night, right before טבילה, is fine.

keyTerms.meaning: It is enough / it will do
Kettles or pots for heating water
Buckets or basins for carrying water
Servants

steps.whatToRemember: רב נחמן בר יצחק holds a woman may wash her hair at night and immerse that same night.

phrases.english: It is enough, come tomorrow,
phrases.notes: She is hinting that she hasn't washed her hair yet, so she can't go to the מקוה tonight.

phrases.english: and he knew what she was saying to him.
He said: Are you missing kettles?
Are you missing buckets?
Are you missing servants?
phrases.notes: He means: you have everything you need, so go wash your hair tonight.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes a story begun earlier on the daf, which serves as evidence about washing at night.
steps.raayaObject: Whether a woman may wash her hair at night right before טבילה.
steps.raayaSupportSource: רב נחמן בר יצחק's reply in the story, telling her to wash right away.

steps.title: רבא: Wash on Friday, immerse Saturday night
steps.stepSummary: רבא publicly teaches that a woman may wash her hair on ערב שבת and immerse on מוצאי שבת.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא taught: A woman may wash her hair on Friday and immerse on Saturday night.
steps.whatsHappening: A new topic begins. רבא gives a public ruling for a woman whose טבילה falls on מוצאי שבת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: She cannot wash her hair on שבת, so רבא lets her wash beforehand, on ערב שבת, even though a whole day goes by before the טבילה. This ruling is about to be challenged.

keyTerms.meaning: Washes her hair, the cleaning done before טבילה
Immerses in the מקוה
Friday, before שבת
Saturday night, after שבת ends

phrases.english: Rava taught publicly:
A woman may wash her hair on Friday
and immerse on Saturday night.

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּרַשׁ רָבָא: אִשָּׁה חוֹפֶפֶת בְּעֶרֶב שַׁבָּת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new discussion about the timing of חפיפה and טבילה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A woman may wash on ערב שבת and immerse on מוצאי שבת.

steps.title: רב פפא: רבין's letter says the opposite
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא challenges רבא with a letter from רבין that rules she may not wash on ערב שבת and immerse on מוצאי שבת.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא said to רבא: But רבין sent in his letter: A woman may not wash on Friday and immerse on Saturday night.
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא attacks רבא's ruling by quoting a ruling from רבין that says exactly the opposite.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבין, who sent rulings from ארץ ישראל, wrote word for word against what רבא just taught. So רבא's ruling seems to go against a known tradition.

keyTerms.meaning: But look! Opens a challenge from a known source
His letter
She may wash her hair

phrases.english: Rav Pappa said to Rava:
But didn't Ravin send in his letter:
"A woman may not wash her hair on Friday
and immerse on Saturday night."

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב פָּפָּא לְרָבָא: וְהָא שְׁלַח רָבִין בְּאִגַּרְתֵּיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Directly challenges רבא's ruling from step 2.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבא's ruling that she may wash on ערב שבת and immerse on מוצאי שבת.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A ruling sent by רבין says the exact opposite.

steps.title: The reason: Immersion must follow washing right away
steps.stepSummary: The letter adds a reason: even washing by day and immersing that night is already surprising, since טבילה must come right after חפיפה.
steps.simpleTranslation: And be amazed at yourself: How can a woman wash by day and immerse at night? We need the immersion right after the washing, and that is missing!
steps.whatsHappening: This explains the reason behind רבין's ruling and makes the challenge against רבא stronger.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rule is that טבילה should come right after חפיפה. Even the usual practice of washing during the day and immersing that night already stretches this rule. So washing on Friday for an immersion on Saturday night stretches it far too much.

keyTerms.meaning: And be amazed at yourself, meaning: this is already surprising
Washing the hair before טבילה
Immersion right after the washing
And that is not there

steps.confusionAlert: The "be amazed" line does not forbid washing by day on a regular weekday. It says even that is already a stretch, so an even longer gap is surely too much.

phrases.english: And be amazed at yourself:
How can she wash by day and immerse at night?
But we require immersion right after washing,
and that is missing!

steps.triggerLanguage: וּתְמַהּ עַל עַצְמְךָ: הֵיאַךְ חוֹפֶפֶת בַּיּוֹם וְטוֹבֶלֶת בַּלַּיְלָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the reason behind רבין's ruling and strengthens רב פפא's challenge.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבא's ruling allowing a full day between חפיפה and טבילה.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: טבילה must come right after חפיפה. If even a few hours is surprising, a whole day is surely not allowed.

steps.title: רבא publicly admits his mistake
steps.stepSummary: רבא appoints an אמורא to announce to the public that his earlier ruling was a mistake.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא then set up an interpreter for himself and taught: The things I told you were a mistake on my part.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא accepts רב פפא's challenge and publicly takes back his ruling.
steps.deeperAnalysis: He did not answer the challenge. Instead he agreed he was wrong. He used an אמורא, the person who repeats the teacher's words aloud to the crowd, so the same public that heard the mistake would hear the correction.

keyTerms.meaning: Set up an interpreter to announce his words aloud to the audience
They were a mistake on my part

steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that a great teacher openly corrects a mistaken ruling in public, in the same way he taught it.

phrases.english: Rava then appointed an interpreter for himself,
and taught: The things I said before you
were a mistake on my part.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: רבא accepts the challenge from steps 3 and 4 and takes back step 2.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: רבא's ruling in step 2 is withdrawn.

steps.title: The correct ruling in רבי יוחנן's name
steps.stepSummary: רבא teaches the correct ruling in the name of רבי יוחנן: she may not wash on ערב שבת and immerse on מוצאי שבת, because טבילה must be close to חפיפה.
steps.simpleTranslation: But this is what they said in רבי יוחנן's name: A woman may not wash on Friday and immerse on Saturday night. And be amazed at yourself: How can she wash by day and immerse at night? We need the immersion close to the washing, and that is missing!
steps.whatsHappening: רבא replaces his mistaken ruling with the correct one, which he quotes from רבי יוחנן. It matches רבין's letter.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The גמרא repeats the full ruling and its reason, now as רבא's own corrected teaching. The reason is said here with the word סמוך, close to, where before it said תכף, right after. Either way, a full day between חפיפה and טבילה is too long.

keyTerms.meaning: However / but in truth
In the name of
Immersion close to the washing

steps.whatToRemember: The final ruling: a woman whose טבילה is on מוצאי שבת should not wash on ערב שבת, because טבילה must come close to חפיפה.

phrases.aramaic: בְּרַם כָּךְ אָמְרוּ מִשְּׁמֵיהּ דְּרַבִּי יוֹחָנָן:
phrases.english: But this is what they said in the name of Rabbi Yochanan:
A woman may not wash her hair on Friday
and immerse on Saturday night,
and be amazed at yourself:
How can she wash by day and immerse at night?
But we require immersion close to washing,
and that is missing!

steps.triggerLanguage: בְּרַם כָּךְ אָמְרוּ מִשְּׁמֵיהּ דְּרַבִּי יוֹחָנָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the corrected ruling that replaces the one רבא just withdrew.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: She may not wash on ערב שבת and immerse on מוצאי שבת, since טבילה must be close to חפיפה.

steps.title: Two practical rulings about when to wash
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא states two rulings: a woman may wash by day and immerse at night, and a woman may wash only at night.
steps.simpleTranslation: The הלכה is: a woman may wash her hair during the day and immerse at night. And the הלכה is: a woman may wash her hair only at night.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא states two practical rulings about the timing of חפיפה. This sets up the next move, where the גמרא will point out that they seem to clash.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Back in step 4, the letter was surprised that she could wash by day and immerse at night. Now the first ruling says this is fine. The second ruling seems to say the opposite: she must wash at night, right before טבילה.

keyTerms.meaning: The practical halacha; the final ruling

phrases.english: And the halacha is:
a woman may wash her hair during the day
and immerse at night.
And the halacha is:
a woman may wash her hair only at night.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהִלְכְתָא: אִשָּׁה חוֹפֶפֶת בַּיּוֹם וְטוֹבֶלֶת בַּלַּיְלָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After רבא's corrected ruling, the גמרא gives practical rulings on the timing of חפיפה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Washing by day and immersing at night is allowed. A separate ruling says to wash only at night.

steps.title: The two rulings seem to contradict
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא points out that one ruling contradicts the other.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is difficult: one הלכה contradicts the other הלכה!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא notices that the two rulings it just stated seem to clash.
steps.deeperAnalysis: One ruling allows washing by day. The other allows washing only at night. Both cannot be true in the same case.

keyTerms.meaning: One halacha contradicts another halacha

phrases.english: It is difficult:
phrases.notes: Some versions have the word in round brackets and some don't. It doesn't change the meaning.

phrases.english: one halacha contradicts the other halacha!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the two rulings of step 7 as inconsistent with each other.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Washing by day and washing only at night cannot both be the halacha.

steps.title: When it is possible and when it is not
steps.stepSummary: Washing by day applies when that is possible, as on a weekday. Washing only at night applies when it is not possible, as when she immerses right after שבת.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is not difficult. This ruling is where it is possible; that ruling is where it is not possible.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that each ruling applies to a different situation.
steps.deeperAnalysis: On a regular weekday she can wash during the day, close to her immersion that night. When she immerses on מוצאי שבת, she cannot wash on ערב שבת (step 6), so she must wash at night right before she immerses.

keyTerms.meaning: It is not difficult; the two sources talk about different cases
Possible

steps.whatToRemember: Normally she may wash by day and immerse at night. When washing by day is not possible, as after שבת, she washes at night right before טבילה.

phrases.english: It is not difficult:
this ruling is where it is possible,
phrases.notes: This is the weekday case, where she can wash during the day shortly before immersing that night.

phrases.english: that ruling is where it is not possible.
phrases.notes: This is the case of immersing after שבת, when she couldn't wash during the day.

steps.triggerLanguage: לָא קַשְׁיָא — הָא דְּאֶפְשָׁר, הָא דְּלָא אֶפְשָׁר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves the contradiction raised in step 8.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Split the cases (אוקימתא): each ruling applies to a different situation
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The two rulings seemed to address the same situation and contradict each other.
steps.terutzMaskana: Washing by day applies when it is possible. Washing only at night applies when it is not, as after שבת.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Washing by day is fine when possible. Otherwise she washes at night just before טבילה.

steps.title: משנה: Pure in the morning, no twilight check, later found impure
steps.stepSummary: A נדה found pure on the morning of her seventh day, skipped the twilight check, and later found blood. She is presumed pure until that later check.
steps.simpleTranslation: A נדה checked herself on the morning of the seventh day and found herself pure. At twilight she did not do the separating check. Days later she checked and found herself impure. She keeps the status of being pure.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins. It describes a נדה who skipped the twilight check that marks the end of her bleeding, and it rules that she is presumed pure.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The proper practice is a check at twilight on the seventh day, called הפסק טהרה. Here she only checked in the morning. Since that last check showed she was pure, we assume she stayed pure. Her status changes only from the later check that found blood.

keyTerms.meaning: Our משנה
A woman in her days of menstrual impurity
In the morning
Twilight, between sunset and nightfall
She separated; she did the check showing her bleeding stopped (הֶפְסֵק טָהֳרָה)
The presumed status of being pure

phrases.english: MISHNA: A menstruating woman who examined herself
on the seventh day in the morning,
and found herself pure,
but at twilight she did not do the separating check,
phrases.notes: This is the check showing her flow has stopped. Without it she immersed anyway.

phrases.english: and after some days she examined herself
and found herself impure:
she keeps the presumed status of being pure.
phrases.notes: So the pure things she touched after going to the מקוה stay pure, apart from the short stretch step 12 explains.

steps.triggerLanguage: נִדָּה שֶׁבָּדְקָה עַצְמָהּ יוֹם שְׁבִיעִי שַׁחֲרִית, וּמָצְאָה טְהוֹרָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new משנה opens a new topic after the חפיפה discussion ends.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A morning check on the seventh day that found her pure keeps her presumed pure until a later check finds blood.

steps.title: משנה: Impure in the morning, no twilight check, later found pure
steps.stepSummary: The reverse case: she found blood on the morning of her seventh day, skipped the twilight check, and later found herself pure. She is presumed impure until that later check.
steps.simpleTranslation: She checked herself on the morning of the seventh day and found herself impure. At twilight she did not do the separating check. Later she checked and found herself pure. She keeps the status of being impure.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה gives the mirror image of the previous case, and the ruling is reversed: she is presumed impure.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Her last check during her נדה days showed blood. So we assume the bleeding continued, and her immersion that night did not work. Her status changes only from the later clean check.

keyTerms.meaning: The presumed status of being impure

steps.whatToRemember: Without a twilight check, the morning check on the seventh day decides her status until the next check. If it was pure she stays pure, and if it was impure she stays impure.
steps.confusionAlert: Don't think the later check decides the days in between. Those days follow the morning check of day seven. The one exception is in the first case: as step 12 explains, the check that finds blood still reaches back a short time (מעת לעת or מפקידה לפקידה).

phrases.english: If she examined herself on the seventh day in the morning
and found herself impure,
and at twilight she did not do the separating check,
and after some time she examined herself
and found herself pure:
she keeps the presumed status of being impure.

steps.triggerLanguage: בָּדְקָה עַצְמָהּ בְּיוֹם שְׁבִיעִי שַׁחֲרִית וּמָצְאָה טְמֵאָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: The mirror case of step 10, with the opposite ruling.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A morning check on the seventh day that found blood keeps her presumed impure until a later clean check.

steps.title: She is presumed pure but still makes items impure retroactively
steps.stepSummary: The משנה limits the 'presumed pure' ruling. She still makes items impure for the past 24 hours, or back to her last check. With a fixed cycle, she makes things impure only from the moment she found blood.
steps.simpleTranslation: But she makes items impure for twenty-four hours back, and from her last check until this check. If she has a fixed cycle, it is enough to count from the time she saw.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה adds a limit to the case from step 10, where she is presumed pure until the bad check. Even then, the items she touched shortly before that check become impure.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'Presumed pure' protects the days after she went to the מקוה. But like any woman who finds blood, she makes impure the טהרות she touched in the 24 hours before. If her last check was more recent, the impurity goes back only to that check. A woman with a fixed cycle (וסת) is assumed to have started bleeding only when she found the blood, so nothing before then becomes impure.

keyTerms.meaning: A 24-hour period, counted back from the moment she found blood
From one check to the next, meaning back to her last clean check
A fixed, regular menstrual cycle
'Her time is enough': she is impure only from the moment she saw, not before

steps.confusionAlert: 'Presumed pure' does not mean nothing becomes impure. The days after the מקוה stay pure, but the short stretch right before the bad check is still treated as impure.

phrases.english: But she makes impure for a twenty-four-hour period,
phrases.notes: Literally 'from time to time'. It means the 24 hours before the check where she found blood.

phrases.english: and from examination to examination.
And if she has a fixed cycle,
her time is enough.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a limit to the 'presumed pure' ruling of step 10
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Though presumed pure, she makes items impure going back 24 hours or to her last check. If she has a וסת, only from the moment she saw.

steps.title: רבי יהודה: no afternoon check means presumed impure
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהודה rules that a woman who did not do her purity check from מנחה time onward on the seventh day is presumed impure.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהודה says: any woman who did not do the check that moves her into purity from מנחה time and later is presumed impure.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יהודה disagrees with the first case of the משנה. He says a morning check is not enough. She must check in the afternoon of the seventh day.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 10 the משנה said a clean morning check keeps her presumed pure. רבי יהודה requires the check to happen late in the day, from מנחה onward. Without it, she has not properly left her impurity, so she stays presumed impure.

keyTerms.meaning: Doing the check that separates her from impurity and moves her into purity
From מנחה time (the afternoon) and later

phrases.english: And Rabbi Yehuda says:
Any woman who did not do the check moving her into purity
from מנחה time and onward,
this woman is presumed impure,

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Argues with the first case of the משנה (step 10)
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Without a check from מנחה onward on the seventh day, she is presumed impure.

steps.title: חכמים: even a day-two check keeps her presumed pure
steps.stepSummary: The חכמים rule that even if her only clean check was on the second day, and she skipped the check at בין השמשות, she is presumed pure until she later finds blood.
steps.simpleTranslation: The חכמים say: even if she checked on the second day of her נדה days and found herself pure, did not check at בין השמשות, and later checked and found blood, she is presumed pure.
steps.whatsHappening: The חכמים answer רבי יהודה and go even further than the first case of the משנה. A clean check early in her days is enough to presume she stayed pure.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יהודה needs an afternoon check on day seven. The חכמים do not even need a check on day seven. One clean check on day two is enough. Once she was found clean, we assume she stayed clean until the check that showed blood.

keyTerms.meaning: On the second day of her נדה days

steps.whatToRemember: The three views of the משנה: the first case needs a clean check on the morning of day seven. רבי יהודה needs a check from מנחה onward. The חכמים accept even one clean check on day two.

phrases.english: And the Rabbis say:
Even on the second day of her menstruation
phrases.notes: Even if this was her only clean check, with nothing on later days.

phrases.english: she checked and found herself pure,
and at twilight she did not do the transition check,
and after some time she checked and found herself impure,
this woman is presumed pure.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Disagrees with רבי יהודה and goes beyond the first case of the משנה
steps.mimraCoreRuling: One clean check, even on day two, keeps her presumed pure until she later finds blood.

steps.title: רב and לוי: a definite זבה or a doubtful זבה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings a dispute. רב says the woman is a definite זבה, and לוי says she is a doubtful זבה.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: It was stated: רב says she is a definite זבה, and לוי says she is a doubtful זבה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins by quoting an argument between רב and לוי about a woman who skipped her check. Enough days passed that she might count as a זבה, and then she found blood.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The question is how sure we are that she saw blood on the days that would make her a זבה. רב treats it as certain, so she is fully a זבה. לוי treats it as only a doubt. Which case in the משנה they mean is not yet clear, and the גמרא asks that next.

keyTerms.meaning: A woman who saw blood on three days in a row outside her regular period time
Definite, certain
Doubtful, uncertain

phrases.english: GEMARA: It was stated:
Rav says: She is a definite זבה,
phrases.notes: A 'big' זבה, one who saw on three days in a row.

phrases.english: and Levi says: She is a doubtful זבה.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens the גמרא with an argument between אמוראים on the משנה
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רב: definite זבה. לוי: doubtful זבה.

steps.title: Which case of the משנה are רב and לוי discussing?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks which clause of the משנה the dispute is about. It rules out the first clause, because there the משנה says she is presumed pure.
steps.simpleTranslation: About which case? If you say the first case, the משנה teaches 'this woman is presumed pure'!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks which case of the משנה רב and לוי are arguing about. It tries the first case and pushes back right away, so it is setting up a search for the right case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the first case, she checked clean on the morning of day seven, and the משנה says she is presumed pure. If she is presumed pure, she cannot be a זבה at all, definite or doubtful. So the dispute cannot be about that case.

keyTerms.meaning: 'On which one?' A question asking which case or clause a statement refers to
'If you say' or 'Shall we say'. Brings up a suggestion that is about to be rejected
The first clause of a משנה
'It teaches'. Points to the actual words of the משנה

phrases.english: To which case does this refer?
If we say it refers to the first clause,
phrases.notes: That is the case from step 10: a clean morning check on day seven, then blood found later.

phrases.english: the משנה teaches: 'This woman is presumed pure'!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks which case the dispute in step 15 refers to
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which clause of the משנה the dispute between רב and לוי is about
steps.kashyaTarget: The suggestion that רב and לוי mean the first clause
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The first clause calls her presumed pure, so she cannot be any kind of זבה.

steps.title: The second clause of the משנה does not fit רב either
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא tries placing the dispute on the second clause of the משנה. לוי's view fits there, but רב's view does not, because her later check came out clean.
steps.simpleTranslation: Maybe the dispute is about the second clause of the משנה. That makes sense for לוי, who calls her a doubtful זבה. But how can רב call her a definite זבה? She checked later and was found pure!
steps.whatsHappening: Step 16 ruled out the first clause of the משנה. Now the גמרא tries the second clause and shows that it fails too.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the second clause, she was impure on the seventh morning, but her later check was clean. That makes her a doubt, which fits לוי's 'doubtful זבה'. Calling her a definite זבה, as רב does, cannot fit a case where she later checked clean.

keyTerms.meaning: On the latter clause (of the משנה)
Granted / it makes sense that…
A woman whose status as a זבה is in doubt
A definite זבה

phrases.english: Rather, [say it is] on the latter clause.
Granted, we can say she is a doubtful זבה,
but a definite זבה as well?
But she checked and found herself pure!

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא אַסֵּיפָא, בִּשְׁלָמָא סְפֵק זָבָה אָמְרִינַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the search from step 16 by testing the second option, the latter clause of the משנה.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects placing the dispute on the latter clause of the משנה.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: Her later check was clean, so רב's 'definite זבה' cannot apply there.

steps.title: The dispute was taught as a separate case
steps.stepSummary: The dispute is not about the משנה. It is about a different case: impure on the seventh morning, no twilight check, and impure again days later.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, the dispute of רב and לוי was taught on its own. A נדה checked herself on the morning of the seventh day and was impure. At twilight she did not check to confirm she had become pure. Days later she checked and was impure. רב says she is a definite זבה, and לוי says she is a doubtful זבה.
steps.whatsHappening: Since neither clause of the משנה works, the גמרא answers that the dispute was a separate teaching about its own case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The new case differs from the משנה's second clause in one detail: here her later check also found her impure. With impurity found both before and after the missed check, רב's 'definite זבה' now makes sense, and לוי still sees room for doubt.

keyTerms.meaning: A teaching that stands on its own, not attached to the משנה

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix this up with the משנה's second clause. There, the later check was pure. Here, the later check was impure, and that is what makes רב's view possible.

phrases.english: Rather, when [the dispute] of Rav and Levi was stated,
it was stated as a teaching on its own:
A נדה who checked herself
on the seventh day in the morning and found herself impure,
and at twilight she did not do the separating check,
and after some days she checked and found herself impure:
Rav said: [She is] a definite זבה,
and Levi said: [She is] a doubtful זבה.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא, כִּי אִיתְּמַר דְּרַב וְלֵוִי שְׁמַעְתָּא בְּאַפֵּי נַפְשַׁהּ אִיתְּמַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves the problem from steps 16 and 17 by separating the dispute from the משנה.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Moves the dispute to a separate case, not attached to either clause of the משנה
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The dispute was about one of the clauses of the משנה.
steps.terutzMaskana: The dispute is about a separate case where she was found impure both before and after the missed twilight check.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that the משנה's rulings and the dispute of רב and לוי cover different cases. That is why they do not contradict each other.

steps.title: The reasons of רב and לוי
steps.stepSummary: רב says impure before and impure after means she was impure the whole time. לוי says maybe the bleeding stopped in between.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב says she is a definite זבה. She was impure at the start and impure now, so she is definitely impure. לוי says she is a doubtful זבה. Maybe the bleeding stopped somewhere in between.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains the reasoning behind each side of the dispute it just described.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב connects the two impure findings and assumes the bleeding went on the whole time in between. לוי says we cannot assume that, because the bleeding may have stopped in the gap and started again. So her status stays a doubt.

keyTerms.meaning: At the start / originally
Definitely impure
She stopped (bleeding)
In between (the two checks)

steps.whatToRemember: רב: impure before plus impure after means impure the whole time, so she is a definite זבה. לוי: the bleeding may have stopped in between, so she is a doubtful זבה.

phrases.english: Rav said: [She is] a definite זבה,
since at the start she was found impure,
and now she is found impure,
[so] she is definitely impure.
And Levi said: [She is] a doubtful זבה,
[since] say she stopped [bleeding] in between.
phrases.notes: He means the gap between the seventh-day morning check and the check days later.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב אָמַר: זָבָה וַדַּאי, כֵּיוָן דְּמֵעִיקָּרָא נִמְצֵאת טְמֵאָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the reasons behind the two rulings stated in step 18.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רב assumes the impurity continued between the two impure findings. לוי allows that the bleeding may have stopped in between, so her status is a doubt.
